hints: Particle A is heavier ($0.3\text{ kg} > 0.1\text{ kg}$), so particle A accelerates downwards and particle B accelerates upwards with the same acceleration $a$.
Apply Newton's second law ($F = ma$) separately to particle A downwards and particle B upwards, using the common string tension $T$.
Add the two equations to eliminate $T$ and solve for $a$, then substitute $a$ back to determine $T$.
walkthrough:
Write the equation of motion for particle A ($0.3\text{ kg}$) moving downwards:
$$0.3g - T = 0.3a \implies 3 - T = 0.3a$$

Write the equation of motion for particle B ($0.1\text{ kg}$) moving upwards:
$$T - 0.1g = 0.1a \implies T - 1 = 0.1a$$

Add the two equations to eliminate $T$ and solve for the acceleration $a$:
$$(3 - T) + (T - 1) = 0.3a + 0.1a$$
$$2 = 0.4a \implies a = \frac{2}{0.4} = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Substitute $a = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ into the equation for B to solve for the tension $T$:
$$T - 1 = 0.1(5) \implies T = 1 + 0.5 = 1.5\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Because particle A has mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ and particle B has mass $0.1\text{ kg}$, particle A accelerates downwards while particle B accelerates upwards. Since the string is light and inextensible and the pulley is smooth, both particles share the same magnitude of acceleration $a$, and the tension $T$ is uniform throughout the string.

Apply Newton's second law ($F_{\text{net}} = ma$) to particle A in the downwards direction. The downward force is its weight $m_A g = 0.3 \times 10 = 3\text{ N}$, and the upward force is the tension $T$:
$$0.3g - T = 0.3a$$
$$3 - T = 0.3a$$

Apply Newton's second law ($F_{\text{net}} = ma$) to particle B in the upwards direction. The upward force is the tension $T$, and the downward force is its weight $m_B g = 0.1 \times 10 = 1\text{ N}$:
$$T - 0.1g = 0.1a$$
$$T - 1 = 0.1a$$

Add both equations together to eliminate the tension $T$:
$$(3 - T) + (T - 1) = 0.3a + 0.1a$$
$$2 = 0.4a$$

Divide both sides by $0.4$ to find the acceleration $a$:
$$a = \frac{2}{0.4} = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Substitute $a = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ into the equation for particle B to find $T$:
$$T - 1 = 0.1(5)$$
$$T - 1 = 0.5$$
$$T = 1.5\text{ N}$$
The acceleration of the particles is $5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and the tension in the string is $1.5\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.Solving Connected Particle Systems: Forms $0.3g - T = 0.3a$ and $T - 0.1g = 0.1a$, solves simultaneously to obtain $a = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $T = 1.5\text{ N}$.

hints: When particle A falls distance $x$ to hit the ground, particle B rises distance $x$, placing B at a height of $2x$ above the ground with speed $v$.
Find $v^2$ at the instant of impact using $v^2 = u^2 + 2ax = 2(5)x = 10x$.
After A hits the ground, the string goes slack and B moves freely under gravity ($a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$) through an additional height $h = 1.2 - 2x$ before coming instantaneously to rest.
walkthrough:
Find the speed squared of the particles when A hits the ground after descending a distance $x$ from rest with $a = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as = 0 + 2 \times 5 \times x = 10x$$

At the instant A lands, B is at a height of $x + x = 2x$ above the ground. The string becomes slack, so B moves vertically under gravity ($a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$) until reaching its maximum height of $1.2\text{ m}$:

The additional height travelled by B under gravity is $h = 1.2 - 2x$. Apply $v_{\text{top}}^2 = v^2 - 2gh$ with $v_{\text{top}} = 0$:
$$0 = v^2 - 2g(1.2 - 2x)$$
$$v^2 = 2 \times 10 \times (1.2 - 2x) = 20(1.2 - 2x)$$

Equate the two expressions for $v^2$ and solve for $x$:
$$10x = 20(1.2 - 2x)$$
$$10x = 24 - 40x$$
$$50x = 24 \implies x = \frac{24}{50} = 0.48$$
teacher_walkthrough: The motion of particle B occurs in two distinct phases: connected acceleration while the string is taut, followed by free flight under gravity after particle A hits the ground and the string becomes slack.

Phase 1 (Connected motion): Particle A descends a distance $x$ to the ground with constant acceleration $a = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$, starting from rest ($u = 0$). Particle B rises by the exact same distance $x$. Using $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$:
$$v^2 = 0^2 + 2(5)(x) = 10x$$
At the moment particle A strikes the ground, particle B is at height $h_1 = x + x = 2x$ above the ground and moving upwards with speed $v$ given by $v^2 = 10x$.

Phase 2 (Free flight under gravity): When particle A comes to rest on the ground, the string goes slack. Particle B now moves upwards solely under gravity with acceleration $a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ until its vertical velocity becomes zero at its highest point.

The greatest height reached by B is given as $1.2\text{ m}$, so the extra height gained during free flight is:
$$h_{\text{free}} = 1.2 - 2x$$

Apply the constant acceleration formula to this free-flight phase, where initial velocity is $v$, final velocity is $0$, and acceleration is $-10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$0^2 = v^2 + 2(-10)(1.2 - 2x)$$
$$0 = v^2 - 20(1.2 - 2x)$$
$$v^2 = 20(1.2 - 2x)$$

ai_rubric.Modelling Piecewise Motion: Uses $v^2 = 2(5)x = 10x$ for the speed when A hits the ground, sets up $v^2 = 2(10)(1.2 - 2x)$, and solves to obtain $x = 0.48$.
